rawReview.evidence: The character construction is RAW-compatible: .references/srd-5.2.1/Character-Creation.md headings “Standard Array,” “Adjust Ability Scores,” “Level 1 Hit Points,” and “Armor Class”; .references/srd-5.2.1/Character-Origins.md headings “Acolyte,” “Sage,” and “Orc”; .references/srd-5.2.1/Classes/Fighter.md and “Rogue.md” level-1 feature headings; .references/srd-5.2.1/Feats.md heading “Magic Initiate”; and .references/srd-5.2.1/Equipment.md headings “Ammunition,” “Armor,” “Shield,” and “Mastery Properties.” The Wolf and Goblin Warrior stat blocks are present in .references/srd-5.2.1/Animals.md heading “Wolf” and .references/srd-5.2.1/Monsters/Monsters-E-G.md heading “Goblin Warrior.” Fixed monster HP and static damage are permitted by .references/srd-5.2.1/Monsters/Overview.md headings “Hit Points” and “Damage Notation.” The synthetic prism can be represented under .references/srd-5.2.1/Rules-Glossary.md heading “Breaking Objects,” which gives objects Poison and Psychic immunity and permits GM-determined object values.
rawReview.critique: The scenario is not closed or executable as written. The Wolf stat block supplies one Bite attack, but “canonical natural melee attacks” does not explicitly name Bite or state how its creature-only Prone rider is handled for the prism object branch; the scenario directs an adjacent Wolf to attack the synthetic prism, so that ordinary-object execution remains unsupported. Rogue Weapon Mastery requires two weapon kinds, but the scenario specifies only a singular matching choice. “Surfaced,” “supported,” “combat-capable,” “movement-ally,” and “ranged-attack enemy” have no defined mapping in the permitted sources; this leaves weapon/armor/loadout, exact skills and languages, both Magic Initiate cantrips, the level-1 spell, spellcasting abilities, component-bearing equipment, Pack Tactics, Sneak Attack, close-combat disadvantage, movement through allies, and Opportunity Attacks unresolved. .references/srd-5.2.1/Playing-the-Game.md heading “Initiative” requires one GM roll shared by identical monsters, so “roll Initiative for all five” must clarify that Wolf A and Wolf B share a roll; tie ordering is also unspecified. “Shortest route,” “nearest,” and the “canonical line” for rack Cover lack tie-break and geometry rules under “Playing on a Grid” and “Cover.” The Goblin’s shield/Two-Handed Shortbow state and use of Nimble Escape are unspecified. Static damage also needs a critical-hit resolution under “Damage and Healing.” Finally, “terminally dead” and “unable to take another supported battle act” are not RAW states and must define treatment of 0-HP characters, Death Saving Throws, Relentless Endurance, and Unconsciousness. ASSUMPTIONS.md — “Modeling Assumptions” does not resolve these gaps.

policyReview.evidence: The artifact uses canonical SRD identities plus the visibly synthetic “glass calibration prism”; it contains no PHB+ source identifiers, names, slugs, prose, headings, page references, or source-to-Mushroom crosswalk. Its remaining wording is independently scenario-authored, with overlap limited to standard rules terminology and mechanic-forced concise phrasing permitted by AUTHORING.md.

contentReview.evidence: The scenario selects Wolf (Wolf A and Wolf B) and Goblin Warrior (Goblin Warrior A) as canonical stat-block identities, and both are included in the supplied availability profile.

sdkCapabilityReview.evidence: The surrounding Character Sheet authoring, stat-block setup, creature-target attacks, movement, damage, and object state are documented. The required Wolf Bite against the synthetic prism is the deliberate unsupported branch for issue #283 ordinary-object targeting: it cannot be treated as a creature target, and the SRD Bite's Prone rider applies only to a Large or smaller creature. The scenario therefore probes, rather than claims support for, this object-target execution boundary.
